title: Navigating the Baby Blues: What's Normal and What's Next
description:
Up to 80% of new parents experience the 'baby blues' within the first few days after birth. This gentle, expert-led lesson walks you through the physiological triggers behind sudden mood shifts — including hormonal changes, sleep deprivation, and the emotional weight of new responsibility.

You'll learn:
• The difference between baby blues and postpartum depression
• Key symptoms to monitor in the first two weeks
• Gentle, practical coping strategies you can start today
• When and how to seek professional support

Remember: experiencing the baby blues does not mean you are failing. It means your body and mind are adjusting to one of life's most profound transitions.

title: Self-Care Isn't Selfish: Basics for New Parents
description:
When you're caring for a newborn around the clock, taking time for yourself can feel impossible — or even guilty. But self-care is the foundation that lets you show up for your baby.

This lesson covers:
• Micro self-care: 5-minute practices that fit between feeds
• Building a realistic daily rhythm (not a rigid schedule)
• Asking for help without feeling like a burden
• Nourishing your body when cooking feels overwhelming

Small, intentional acts of care add up. You deserve gentleness too.

title: Supporting Your Partner Through the Postpartum Period
description:
The postpartum period reshapes every relationship in the household. Whether you're the birthing parent or the supporting partner, learning to communicate needs clearly and compassionately is essential.

In this lesson you'll explore:
• Recognising signs your partner may be struggling
• Active listening techniques for emotionally charged moments
• Dividing responsibilities without keeping score
• Creating a 'check-in' ritual that keeps you connected

Strong partnerships aren't built on perfection — they're built on showing up, even imperfectly.

title: Sleep When Sleep Is Scarce: Survival Strategies
description:
Sleep deprivation is one of the hardest parts of early parenthood, and it affects everything — mood, patience, decision-making, and physical health.

This lesson offers evidence-based strategies:
• Sleep hygiene basics adapted for new-parent life
• Power-nap techniques that actually restore energy
• Managing nighttime wake-ups as a team
• When fatigue crosses the line into a health concern

You can't pour from an empty cup. Let's find ways to refill yours.

title: Building Your Bond: Connection Activities for Every Day
description:
Bonding with your baby doesn't always happen in a single magical moment. For many parents, it's a gradual process — and that's completely normal.

This lesson explores:
• Skin-to-skin contact and why it matters beyond the first hour
• Talking, singing, and reading to your newborn
• Responsive caregiving: following your baby's cues
• What to do if bonding feels difficult or delayed

Every gentle touch, every whispered word, every quiet moment together is building a bond that will last a lifetime.
